Welcome…
A huge welcome from all of us at Hawthorn Independent Special School. Here at Hawthorn we offer a bespoke service to young people who are experiencing trauma and mental health difficulties.
Young people who come to us usually can’t or don’t attend mainstream schools because of the nature of their mental health problems has left them unable to engage with normal day to day activities. These young people often can’t cope with large environments, noise or strange people. They are unable to engage in mainstream education or even with family at times and become disassociated, anxious, aggressive or distressed very quickly.
Find Out More About What We Do:
Our Mission
We aim to provide young people with the oppertunity to re-engage with education, society and find inspiration for life!
Our Values
At Hawthorn we give young people a voice and allow them to be heard. We support and help them with strategies to overcome the mental health issues that have hindered their personal and educational development.
Our cohort will have missed a significant amount of core education and are unable to catch up or re-join mainstream school.
We concentrate on developing a healthy mind, building resilience and finding strategies that work for the individual.
We aim to ignite a thirst for education once the mind is calm enough to learn.
A message from the Chair…
“All young people deserve the right to an education regardless of the challenges that they face.
We aim to teach our young people the skills that will prepare them for life, and an education tailored to their needs, so that employment and a positive place in society becomes part of their onward journey.”
“I can’t speak highly enough about Chalkhill farm. Julie and her team are incredibly kind, and experienced with supporting young people. They work so hard to care for the children that attend (and their animals.) Being outside in the fresh air with staff that show respect, patience and genuine affection for their attendees leads to a huge improvement in feelings of well being and self esteem. We are so pleased we found this amazing place.“
– Karen Wilson (Google Review)

Curriculum
Our Curriculum
At Hawthorn we put the social, emotional and mental health needs of our pupils before all else, as we understand that our young people need time to engage effectively with education. While learning will always be taking place, we will introduce academic and formal learning gradually and specially targeted towards the needs and interests in a tailored package to suit each individual.
Hawthorn will provide a curriculum, which inspires, challenges and safeguards all our pupils, and enables them to become successful learners, confident individuals and responsible citizens, who are able to live safe, healthy and fulfilling lives.
Subjects and Academic Development
The Aims of Our Curriculum
Our curriculum will provide differentiation and reactive teaching to engage pupils by integrating education and life skills. This will prepare them for adult life within a nurturing, therapeutic, outdoor environment.
We will incorporate Modern British Values which are Democracy, Rule of Law, Respect and Tolerance and Individual Liberty. This will provide all pupils with a balanced view of the world, accepting of all people regardless of gender, religion and ethnic origin; helping them find their own place within society.
Our subjects include:
Physical Education
Art and Design
Land Management and Horticulture
Personal Social and Health Education
Life skills
Animal care
Horse riding
Nature education

Admissions
Admissions
Admissions are made via referrals to Hawthorn from the local authority’s placement process for Independent Special Schools.
We have a very small cohort, offering one-to-one, two-to-one and small group learning. Places are limited, our maxium student intake is currently eight.
Young People will be aged 11 to 18 years old.
We are able to support neurodiverse pupils with an EHCP who have social, emotional, mental ill health needs.
Hawthorn will need to meet the needs of the individual before the admission is finalised.

Activities
Theraputic Education
Each young person develops individually and dependent upon their needs the activities will be tailored personally. Learning new skills are often very subliminal which removes the fear of failure and enables each young person to build resilience to re-engage with learning and life. We have several options available to suit the needs of young people.
The School Day involves various activities to encourage working with peers, following instructions, being able to think and work as an individual and taking on small amounts of responsibility. There is no stress involved but everyone is expected to try their best and include themselves with all tasks. We use the emotional age of the individual rather than the physical age and a holistic approach based on THRIVE which provides a safe nurturing environment. An example of this is a young person with adverse childhood experiences, attachment or trauma -based problems, is often unable to recognize their physical and emotional needs such as feeling cold, needing to have a drink or removing themselves from hazards. We use the online THRIVE assessments to assess and monitor progress.
Activities shall be combined with education and tailored to functional skills and a horse/animal care qualification, incorporating the national curriculum of Maths, English and ICT. For those who wish to pursue further qualifications this can be accommodated to the individuals specific skill set or career choice.
Woodcraft & Maintenance
Wildlife & Nature Activities
Our wildlife garden provides a varied habitat for migrating and nesting birds. Birds that visit include kestrels, buzzards, peregrine falcons, a red kite, goldfinches, pied wagtails and goldcrests. We have nest boxes and bug houses throughout the site and our annual nesting swallows reside in our stables.
We raise caterpillars, study bugs and their lifecycles and this gives young people the opportunity to be hands on and understand the importance of various habitats and the environment. Our wildlife pond attracts dragonflies, frogs and newts and provides an important source of drinking water for local birds, insects and mammals.
One To One Approach
In our experience young people who struggle with a full week in mainstream schools with mental health problems who need to build life skills and resilience benefit from one to one teaching and therapeutic sessions. This may include equine assisted therapy, therapeutic arts and crafts or regulation strategies.
Peer Group Learning
These are small group sessions divided into suitable groups for pupils who need to go further back into their reintroduction to education and life skills. Usually they have trauma related problems that have caused regressive behaviour and a chaotic brain needing a more finely tuned therapeutic approach while the child begins to heal.
Our student groups are four to eight. This means that we meet the needs of each individual while they are recovering and rebuilding. School Days are from 9:00 till 2:30.
Students will need to bring with them a packed- lunch and suitable clothes for the weather.
